## Mole-fraction state and its mixture totals (`ThermoX`) {#sec-ch03-thermo-x}

### Summary

Column models, adiabat construction and most offline analysis describe a parcel by temperature, pressure and mole
fractions, $(T, p, x)$. `ThermoX` works on that state. It converts mole fractions to concentrations and mass
fractions, computes density, heat capacity at constant pressure, enthalpy and entropy per unit volume, and inverts
the entropy for temperature at fixed pressure. Its `forward` method, the saturation adjustment at fixed temperature
and pressure, is the subject of @sec-ch04.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Conversions of the $(T, p, x)$ state; the mixture totals @eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $x_n$ [-] for all species; concentrations $c_n$ [mol m$^{-3}$].

**Placement.** Used by adiabat construction (@sec-ch03-adiabat) and by callers working in $(T, p, x)$.

**Activation.** API: `ThermoX(options)`, then `compute("<from>-><to>", [...])`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact except `TPX->V` with $z_n \ne 1$; `PXS->T` can return a wrong $T$ (Limits).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $C_p$, heat capacity at constant pressure per unit volume [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$]; $H$,
enthalpy per unit volume [J m$^{-3}$]; $\rho$, $y_n$, $c_n$, $x_n$, $N_{\mathrm g}$ as in @sec-ch03-thermo-y and
@sec-ch03-eos. Local symbols: $S$, entropy per unit volume [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\mu_n$ as in @sec-ch03-thermo-y.

The `compute` keys are named by inputs and output: `V` is the vector of concentrations $c_n$ here (not partial
densities as in `ThermoY`), `D` the density, `X` the mole fractions, `Y` the mass fractions.

### Derivation

**Mass fractions and density.** From $\rho_n = \mu_n c_n = \mu_n x_n c$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_n &= \frac{x_n \mu_n}{\sum_k x_k \mu_k}, \quad n \ge 1, \\
\rho &= \sum_n c_n \mu_n .
\end{aligned}
$$

`X->Y` computes the first line in `_xfrac_to_yfrac`; `V->D` the second in `_conc_to_dens`. Concentrations come
from @eq-ch03-eos-conc (`TPX->V`).

**Mixture totals.** As in @sec-ch03-thermo-y, each total is a concentration-weighted sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_p &= \sum_n c_n c_{p,n}(T), \\
H &= \sum_n c_n h_n(T), \\
S &= \sum_n c_n s_n(T, p) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals}

The lines are computed in `_cp_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_cp_vol >}}), `_enthalpy_vol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_enthalpy_vol >}}) and `_entropy_vol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_entropy_vol >}}). `THS->G` returns the Gibbs energy $H - T S$.

**Temperature from entropy at fixed pressure.** `PXS->T` solves $S(T) = S_{\mathrm{given}}$ for the entropy per
unit volume $S$ of @eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals, recomputing the concentrations from @eq-ch03-eos-conc at every
iterate. At fixed $p$ and $x$ every concentration scales as $1/T$, so $\partial c_n / \partial T = -c_n / T$. For a
gas, $\partial s_n / \partial T = c_{p,n} / T$ at fixed $p$ and $x_n$. For a condensate, whose entropy is solved from
saturation, the same holds when its card matches its saturation curve (@eq-ch03-reference-state-sc-slope). Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial S}{\partial T} &= \sum_n \frac{\partial c_n}{\partial T} s_n + \sum_n c_n \frac{\partial s_n}{\partial T}
= -\frac{S}{T} + \frac{C_p}{T} , \\
\frac{\partial S}{\partial T} &= \frac{C_p - S}{T} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-slope}

Newton's method on $S(T) = S_{\mathrm{given}}$ with this slope is

$$
T \leftarrow T + T\, \frac{S_{\mathrm{given}} - S(T)}{C_p(T) - S(T)} ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-correct}

This is Newton's method at frozen composition. Its result does not depend on the entropy constants, because $S$ and
$C_p - S$ shift together, and for a parcel in which nothing condenses it converges quadratically (check line `(f3)`).
In a saturated parcel it does not. Each `PXS->T` pass calls `forward`, so $S(T)$ is taken along the equilibrium path,
and its true slope there carries the latent heat, $(C_{p,\mathrm{eff}} - S)/T$ with the effective heat capacity of
@sec-ch03-adiabat. With the frozen slope the map's derivative at the root is

$$
1 - \frac{C_p - S}{C_{p,\mathrm{eff}} - S} ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-frozen-factor}

which is not zero once anything condenses, so the convergence is only linear.
An equivalent route is to invert the molar entropy, as the adiabat does (@sec-ch03-adiabat). At the
pin the code does not use this slope. Its update, computed in `_entropy_to_temp`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_entropy_to_temp >}}), is

$$
T \leftarrow T \left(1 + \frac{S_{\mathrm{given}} - S(T)}{C_p(T)}\right) ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-newton}

which, at frozen composition, is Newton's method for an entropy per mole or per kilogram (slope $C_p/T$), not per
volume. Write the update
as $T \leftarrow \phi(T)$ with $\phi(T) = T + T (S_{\mathrm{given}} - S)/C_p$. At a root $T^{\ast}$,
$S = S_{\mathrm{given}}$, so

$$
\phi'(T^{\ast}) = 1 - \frac{T^{\ast}}{C_p} \frac{\partial S}{\partial T} = 1 - \frac{C_p - S}{C_p} = \frac{S}{C_p}
= \frac{\bar s}{\bar c_p} ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-factor}

with $\bar s = S / \sum_n c_n$ and $\bar c_p = C_p / \sum_n c_n$ per mole of mixture. Three consequences follow.
(1) The iteration converges only where $\lvert \bar s / \bar c_p \rvert < 1$, and only linearly. (2) $\bar s$
contains the arbitrary entropy constants `s0_R` and the reference state $T_\star$, $p_\star$
(@sec-ch03-reference-state), so whether `PXS->T` converges depends on constants that should not change any
physical answer. (3) By @eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-slope, $S(T)$ at fixed $p$ has a turning point where
$S = C_p$, so a given $S_{\mathrm{given}}$ can have a second, spurious root, to which the iteration may converge.
The adiabat code avoids all three by inverting the molar entropy $\bar s$ instead (@sec-ch03-adiabat). This is the
defect D8.[^ch03-d8] Its fix steps in $\ln T$. The first step uses the frozen slope, $C_p - S$ per volume, as in
@eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-correct. Later steps use a secant slope between successive iterates along the equilibrium
path, which carries the latent heat, and fall back to the frozen slope when the secant is zero or not finite.
Converged columns are frozen, and columns that are NaN stay active. How fast the fixed code converges, and whether
check line `(f4)` passes on it within the allowed passes, is not measured here (no build of the fix branch was run).
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-newton code at the pin, not the correct step (D8) -->

After each step the code calls `forward`, the saturation adjustment at the new $(T, p)$, which changes the
composition in place. The slope $C_p$ is also frozen: it omits the latent heat of the condensation that `forward`
adds or removes (the effective heat capacity of @sec-ch03-adiabat would include it).

### Numerical method

Every conversion is pointwise. `PXS->T` starts from $T = T_\star$ (`Tref`) in every cell and iterates
@eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-newton until $\max \lvert 1 - T_{\mathrm{old}}/T_{\mathrm{new}} \rvert$ is below `ftol` or `max_iter`
iterations are spent. Each iteration converts $x$ to $c$, evaluates $C_p$ and $S$, and runs one saturation
adjustment. `TPX->V` iterates only when a compressibility function is set (@sec-ch03-eos).

Tensor layout: mole fractions and concentrations are `(..., 1 + ny)` with the species last; mass fractions are
`(ny, ...)`, as in `ThermoY`.

The `ThermoX` figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of `ThermoX`. {#tbl-ch03-thermo-x-code}

Setup checks and warnings a user can hit: `X->Y` refuses an input whose species count is not the module's; an
unknown key is refused; `PXS->T` and `TPX->V` warn when `max_iter` is reached. On that warning both also write
their inputs to a file `thermo_x_entropy_to_temp_<time>.pt` or `thermo_x_xfrac_to_conc_<time>.pt` in the working
directory (verified by reading `_entropy_to_temp` and `_xfrac_to_conc` at the pin). `PXS->T` overwrites the mole
fractions it is given with the equilibrated ones.

### Limits

`PXS->T` returns wrong temperatures, not merely slow ones, away from $T_\star$. The content review of this
chapter, run on kintera built at the pin, measured[^ch03-pxs-review] for a dry parcel at 1 bar started at
$T_\star = 300$ K: target 600 K gave 594.16 K with `max-iter` 10 and 599.9987 K with 100; target 150 K gave NaN
(the first step makes $T < 0$); with `s0_R` 5 and target 600 K it converged to 103.78 K, the spurious root; with
`s0_R` 15.7 or 30 it gave NaN or overflow. In saturated parcels of `tests/jupiter.yaml` equilibrated at $T_\star$
and 1 bar the same review measured: 5 % H$_2$O, $T_\star = 300$ K, returned 321.605 K with `max-iter` 10 and 100;
the Jupiter composition at 150 K returned NaN; 5 % H$_2$O at 280 K returned 280.871 K (10) and 280.0001 K (100).
The 600 K case with `max-iter` 10 is rerun by check line `(f4)` (594.1625594 K, D8); the other numbers are the
review's measurements and were not rerun for this text. They agree with
@eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-factor: only a start at the answer is exact, and the frozen slope adds a latent-heat
error in saturated parcels. The only test of `PXS->T` starts at $T_\star$, where the answer is the start.

When `max_iter` is reached, `PXS->T` warns, writes its inputs to a file, and returns the last iterate; the caller
cannot tell a converged result from an unconverged one except by the warning. It also mutates its mole-fraction
argument. Each iteration runs the saturation adjustment of @sec-ch04 with the same `max-iter`; a cell that the
adjustment leaves unconverged gives `PXS->T` a composition off saturation, and `ThermoX.forward` keeps no failure
count (verified by reading `ThermoXImpl::forward`, {{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::forward >}}). The
file written on non-convergence lands in the working directory of the caller.
